full_translation_en:
Federal Parliament
House of Representatives, 2082
Second Session
Meeting Number - 43
Federal Parliament of Nepal
Notice Paper - 2
(Brief Minutes of the Meeting Proceedings)
Tuesday, Shrawan 26, 2083
The meeting of the House of Representatives commenced today at 1:15 PM under the chairmanship of the Honorable Speaker Dol Prasad Aryal.
At the beginning of the meeting, when Honorable Members from Nepali Congress, Nepal Communist Party (UML), Nepal Communist Party, Labor Culture Party, and Rastriya Prajatantra Party stood in front of their seats and sought time to speak, the Honorable Speaker granted time to the following Honorable Members, who then expressed their objections to the government and the Prime Minister's working style, drew the government's attention to issues of border disputes, administrative delays, and corruption. The Honorable Prime Minister was urged to come to the House in national attire, to provide a response in the House regarding national problems and border encroachment, and to remove the Prime Minister's statement from the parliamentary record. They also spoke on issues such as the need to enact laws to provide strict punishment to criminals for the end of widespread irregularities, corruption, impunity, and injustice in the country, and the government and ruling coalition parties' inability to be responsible for national sovereignty, a clear foreign policy, and the resolution of citizens' basic problems.
1. Hon. Harkaraj Rai
2. Hon. Bharat Kumar Swar
3. Hon. Chandeshwor Mandal
4. Hon. Bharat Giri
5. Hon. Gopal Sharma
Subsequently, after Hon. Harkaraj Rai finished speaking, Hon. Inder Rana Magar raised a point of order, stating that the word "core hanne" (to hit the core) used by the Honorable Member during his speech was inhumane and that the use of such harsh words was contrary to democracy and human rights, and demanded that the word be removed from the parliamentary record.
Following that, Honorable Ninu Kumari Karna took emergency time to express heartfelt tribute and condolences to the late Radhika Gotame, Prashant Adhikari, and Dr. Nutan Sharma, who passed away this morning in Janakpur, and extended sympathy to the bereaved families. She also expressed condolences on the passing of Radhika Gotame, Prashant Adhikari, and Dr. Nutan Sharma. She also expressed condolences on the passing of the late litterateur, poet, and novelist Rajendra Bimal, and extended sympathy to the bereaved family.

Subsequently, after Hon. Purna Prasad Limbu finished speaking, Hon. Smriti Senchury took emergency time and demanded justice for the victim and legal action against the perpetrators for luring a 17-year-old minor girl, administering hormonal injections, and other such acts.
Similarly, Hon. Madan Krishna Shrestha took emergency time and demanded an impartial investigation into the death of Umesh Khadgi at the reform center in Sirutar, Bhaktapur.
Subsequently, after Hon. Harimohan Bhandari finished speaking, Hon. Parvati BK raised a point of order, objecting to the previous speaker's statement that "leaders are full of scandals," and demanded clarification on which leaders were full of scandals. Similarly, Hon. Harkaraj Rai raised a point of order, stating that the word "leaders have engaged in corruption" used by Hon. Harimohan Bhandari during his speech was unparliamentary, demanded that the government investigate and take action against the guilty, and that the word be removed from the parliamentary record.
Thereafter, the Honorable Minister of Industry, Commerce, and Supplies, Gauri Kumari, presented a proposal for consideration of the "Mining and Minerals Bill, 2083."
Following that, the Honorable Minister of Industry, Commerce, and Supplies, Gauri Kumari, responded to the questions raised by the following Honorable Members during the discussion on the bill:-

Thereafter, the Honorable Speaker presented the proposal "Mining and Minerals Bill, 2083" for decision. Honorable Nishkal Rai raised a point of order regarding the lack of quorum in the House. The Honorable Speaker, in accordance with Article 94 of the Constitution of Nepal, stated that one-fourth of the members of the House of Representatives must be present to present any question or proposal for decision, and directed the Secretariat to ascertain the quorum. After the ringing of the notice bell for 3 minutes and counting the number of present Honorable Members, it was found that the required quorum was 69, but only 61 Honorable Members were present. Therefore, the decision on the proposal to consider the bill will be made in the next meeting.
Subsequently, the next meeting of the House of Representatives will be held on Monday, Bhadra 1, 2083, at 1:00 PM, and the House adjourned at 5:05 PM.
Padma Prasad Pandey
Secretary

sections.summary_en: The proposal to consider the "Mining and Minerals Bill, 2083" was presented. A point of order was raised regarding the lack of quorum. The count revealed 61 members present, falling short of the required 69. The decision on the bill was postponed to the next meeting.

sections.summary_en: The House of Representatives adjourned its meeting until Monday, Bhadra 1, 2083, at 1:00 PM.
